title: PerovAgent: Autonomous Ligand Design for Halide Perovskite Nanocrystals
authors: Seungjun Cha, Yoo Jae Jeong, Amanda Conde Del Moral, Juan-Pablo Correa-Baena, Seth R. Marder, David S. Ginger
abstract: Designing surface-capping ligands for high-performance halide perovskite nanocrystals requires navigating a vast molecular space while discovering design rules that govern ligand-surface interactions. Here, we introduce PerovAgent, an autonomous multi-agent framework that combines large language model (LLM)-driven scientific reasoning with computational tools for atomistic model construction, machine-learned interatomic potential evaluation, and statistical validation. Across ten independent campaigns on CsPbBr3 surfaces, PerovAgent adaptively explored and refined diverse ligand chemistries while progressively improving the binding-energy objective. Beyond optimization, the framework converts recurring chemical observations into explicit design principles that can be statistically evaluated. Of 35 formulated principles, 19 were prospectively supported, of which seven also passed the confound audit, highlighting the need to systematically validate plausible LLM-generated hypotheses during autonomous discovery. A recurrent alkynyl-phosphonate principle was further examined using density functional theory, which reproduced the predicted energetic preference. These results demonstrate an autonomous discovery framework that not only searches molecular space and optimizes the scalar objective but also transforms its search trajectory into systematically testable design principles. The framework can also be extended to more complex ligands, including zwitterionic, multidentate, and polymerizable ligands, to explore a wider range of ligand-surface interactions and uncover new design principles for halide perovskite nanocrystals.

infographic.key_insight: PerovAgent autonomously designs ligands for halide perovskite nanocrystals while turning its search history into statistically testable chemical design principles.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The framework could guide surface-capping ligand selection by optimizing binding energies and identifying validated ligand–surface interaction rules.
method: Coordinate LLM-driven reasoning with atomistic model construction and machine-learned interatomic potential evaluation.
Adaptively explore ligand chemistries on CsPbBr3 surfaces to improve the binding-energy objective.
Formulate design principles, test them prospectively, and audit for confounding.
infographic.evidence_signal: Across 10 independent campaigns, 19 of 35 principles gained prospective support, seven of those passed the confound audit, and DFT reproduced the energetic preference predicted by a recurrent alkynyl-phosphonate principle.
infographic.watch_item: Improved computed binding energies do not establish experimental nanocrystal performance, and many plausible principles did not survive validation.
infographic.paper_title: PerovAgent: Autonomous Ligand Design for Halide Perovskite Nanocrystals

title: Graph Neural Networks for Accurate Quasiparticle Energy Levels in Large Supercells of Transition Metal Dichalcogenides
authors: Rafael R. Del Grande, David A. Strubbe
abstract: The GW method is the one of the main workhorses of the materials science community to accurately calculate the electronic bandgap of materials, as it overcomes the gap underestimation problem from Density Functional Theory (DFT). Despite its accuracy, its computational cost becomes prohibitive when calculations have more than 10-100 atoms, which makes more difficult its use for defects, surfaces and moiré systems that demand large supercells. To overcome this problem, we developed a Graph Neural Network trained with smaller GW calculations which can make accurate predictions on large supercells at a small fraction of the computational cost. Our model uses as features the projection of DFT wavefunctions into localized atomic orbitals, while graph nodes represent the atomic positions and edges represent atom to atom distances, which captures the system geometry. We explore how to do "small AI", providing a workflow of how to create a personal and convenient dataset of GW calculations to train the model that can be applied to different materials so that the final user does not need to rely on massive datasets. We define what must be included in the training dataset to capture the physics of our objective simulation, and perform a Bayesian optimization of hyperparameters. In the case of monolayer MoS$_2$ with a sulfur vacancy our GNN models achieve high accuracy (MAE ranging 10 to 50 meV) with a simplified workflow applicable to other materials, accelerating accurate large electronic structure calculations.

infographic.key_insight: A graph neural network trained on smaller GW calculations predicts quasiparticle energy levels in large supercells at a fraction of the computational cost.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The approach could make accurate electronic-structure calculations more practical for defects, surfaces, and moiré systems where conventional GW becomes costly.
method: Represent atoms as graph nodes and interatomic distances as edges.
Use DFT wavefunction projections onto localized atomic orbitals as input features.
Build a targeted, compact GW training dataset and optimize hyperparameters with Bayesian optimization.
infographic.evidence_signal: For monolayer MoS₂ with a sulfur vacancy, the abstract reports mean absolute errors of 10–50 meV.
infographic.watch_item: Accuracy depends on representative GW training data; transferability beyond the reported MoS₂ vacancy case is not established in the abstract.
infographic.paper_title: Graph Neural Networks for Accurate Quasiparticle Energy Levels in Large Supercells of Transition Metal Dichalcogenides

title: Effects of Yttrium doping on Proton Conductivity in Ba(Fe, Co, Zr, Y)O$_{3-δ}$ Cathode Materials for Proton Ceramic Fuel Cells
authors: Chiyoung Kim, Ryan Jacobs, Jun Meng, Jack H. Duffy, Kyle S. Brinkman, Yueh-Lin Lee
abstract: Protonic ceramic fuel cells (PCFCs) offer efficient energy conversion at intermediate temperatures, but their performance is often constrained by sluggish oxygen reduction kinetics at the cathode. Triple conducting perovskite materials such as BaCo$_x$Fe$_y$Zr$_z$Y$_{1-x-y-z}$O$_{3-δ}$ (BCFZY) have shown promise as air electrodes. In this study, we investigated the impact of Y doping on proton conductivity by decoupling the effects on proton diffusivity and proton concentration. Using ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations, we assessed proton tracer diffusivity across three compositions: BaCo$_{0.4}$Fe$_{0.4}$Zr$_{0.2}$O$_{3-δ}$ (BCFZ), BaCo$_{0.4}$Fe$_{0.4}$Zr$_{0.1}$Y$_{0.1}$O$_{3-δ}$ (BCFZY0.1) and BaCo$_{0.4}$Fe$_{0.4}$Y$_{0.2}$O$_{3-δ}$ (BCFY). Thermodynamic defect models incorporating hydration, oxidation, and hydride formation reactions are employed to estimate temperature-dependent proton concentrations. Our results suggest that increasing the Y content from BCFZ to BCFY increases proton diffusivity by 1.7% at 500 $^\circ$C. Under PCFC operating gas conditions, proton concentration and proton conductivity are predicted to increase by 3.8% and 5.3%, respectively, at 500 $^\circ$C. These increases are modest compared with the larger enhancements reported experimentally under reducing conditions, highlighting the importance of gas conditions in evaluating the effects of Y doping. Under low oxygen partial pressure conditions, we predict that the dominant proton transport mechanism shifts from hydroxyl groups (OH$_O^{\bullet}$) to hydride species (H$_O^{\bullet}$). This work provides mechanistic insight into proton transport in BCFZY cathodes and offers design principles for optimizing proton-conducting air electrodes in next-generation PCFCs.

infographic.key_insight: Replacing Zr with Y in BCFZY cathodes yields modest proton-conductivity gains under PCFC operating gases, while low oxygen partial pressure is predicted to shift proton transport from hydroxyl to hydride species.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Cathode optimization should account for gas-dependent defect chemistry rather than assume Y doping alone will substantially improve proton conductivity.
method: Used ab initio molecular dynamics to evaluate proton tracer diffusivity in BCFZ, BCFZY0.1, and BCFY.
Modeled temperature-dependent proton concentrations using hydration, oxidation, and hydride-formation defect reactions.
Separated diffusivity and concentration contributions to proton conductivity.
infographic.evidence_signal: At 500 °C, increasing Y content from BCFZ to BCFY predicts gains of 1.7% in proton diffusivity, 3.8% in proton concentration, and 5.3% in proton conductivity under PCFC operating gas conditions.
infographic.watch_item: These simulation-based predictions are gas-condition dependent and should not be generalized to the larger experimental enhancements reported under reducing conditions.
infographic.paper_title: Effects of Yttrium doping on Proton Conductivity in Ba(Fe, Co, Zr, Y)O$_{3-δ}$ Cathode Materials for Proton Ceramic Fuel Cells

title: DeepDOSReasoner: Physics-Grounded Reasoning for Density-of-States Prediction and Materials Discovery
authors: Yingheng Wang, Francesco Ricci, Zhilong Wang, Tao Yu, Junwen Bai, Xiangyun Lei
abstract: Predicting a material's behavior from its atomic structure is a longstanding goal of the physical sciences. The electronic and phonon densities of states (eDOS and phDOS) govern key electronic, optical, vibrational, and thermodynamic properties, yet their calculation using density functional theory (DFT) is costly: about 60% of Materials Project entries lack eDOS and over 80% lack phDOS. Existing crystal-to-spectrum models rely on pooled structural representations and pointwise regression, which blur spectral features and violate total-state conservation. Here we introduce DeepDOSReasoner, a physics-grounded framework that decodes spectra through atom-to-energy source attention and refines the normalized DOS through learned continuity-equation transport, enforcing nonnegativity and total-state conservation by construction. DeepDOSReasoner achieves the highest prediction accuracy across all evaluated metrics for both eDOS and phDOS, recovers element-resolved contributions without supervision, and most reliably identifies rare valence-band (VB) gaps. In a prospective screen of 8,106 uncharted materials validated by new DFT calculations, its predictions remain the most accurate among the methods evaluated, with 25 of its top 50 candidates confirmed as VB-gap materials. Three case studies spanning substituted compounds, photovoltaic chalcogenides, and a high-entropy alloy demonstrate transfer across materials classes. Ablations confirm that both stages are necessary, while the model retains comparable accuracy when trained on only 25% of the data. Predicting spectra in milliseconds enables exhaustive screening; we release predictions filling the missing eDOS for 91,405 and phDOS for 127,768 Materials Project entries. DeepDOSReasoner provides a blueprint for integrating machine learning with physical reasoning toward high-throughput spectral screening and autonomous materials discovery.

infographic.key_insight: DeepDOSReasoner predicts electronic and phonon density-of-states spectra while enforcing nonnegativity and total-state conservation by construction.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Millisecond-scale spectral prediction enables high-throughput screening for electronic, optical, vibrational, and thermodynamic materials properties.
method: Decode spectra from crystal structures using atom-to-energy source attention.
Refine normalized spectra through learned continuity-equation transport.
Recover element-resolved contributions without direct supervision.
infographic.evidence_signal: The model led all evaluated metrics for both spectrum types; prospective DFT validation across a screen of 8,106 materials confirmed valence-band gaps in 25 of its top 50 candidates.
infographic.watch_item: Physics constraints ensure nonnegative, state-conserving spectra, but do not guarantee accuracy for unfamiliar chemistries; priority candidates still need DFT validation.
infographic.paper_title: DeepDOSReasoner: Physics-Grounded Reasoning for Density-of-States Prediction and Materials Discovery

title: Foundation interatomic potentials capture structural disorder in metallic glasses
authors: Dario Massa, Luca Leoni, Antoni Wadowski, Kacper Cybinski, Anshul D. S. Parmar, Carmine Autieri
abstract: Foundation machine-learning interatomic potentials transfer well across chemical and structural space, yet their reliability for highly disordered metallic states is less established. Metallic glasses are a demanding benchmark: they have traditionally been modeled with Embedded Atom Method (EAM) potentials fitted to specific compositions, while ab initio molecular dynamics remains too expensive at the required sizes and timescales. Using the prototypical Cu-Zr-Al glass, we show that foundation potentials capture structural disorder, reproducing the structure, quenching dynamics, and elastic, mechanical and thermal properties of the amorphous state at near first-principles accuracy. We benchmark MACE foundation models against a classical EAM potential along molecular dynamics quenches, validating against density functional theory and experiment, first at Cu46Zr46Al8 and then across the good glass-forming region of the ternary. We further test two specialization routes: fine-tuning on glass structures generated with Lennard-Jones surrogate models, and on automatically generated small periodic cells (ASSYST). Models pre-trained on databases that include non-equilibrium liquid and amorphous configurations, such as OMAT, are accurate and transferable across composition out of the box, clearly outperforming the composition-specific EAM potential. Fine-tuning on target glass structures brings only modest gains, while specialization on small crystalline cells degrades the description of disorder. The readiness of foundation potentials for disordered metals is therefore set mainly by the diversity of their pre-training data rather than by system-specific fine-tuning, shifting the modeling effort from bespoke dataset generation to pre-training coverage and careful validation of the resulting dynamics.

infographic.key_insight: Foundation interatomic potentials capture disorder in Cu–Zr–Al metallic glasses most reliably when their pre-training includes liquid and amorphous structures.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Broadly pre-trained potentials can reduce reliance on composition-specific models for simulating metallic-glass structure and properties, provided their dynamics are carefully validated.
method: Benchmark MACE foundation models against EAM during molecular-dynamics quenches.
Validate at Cu46Zr46Al8 and across the ternary’s good glass-forming region using DFT and experiment.
Test fine-tuning on surrogate-generated glass structures and ASSYST-generated small periodic cells.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports that OMAT-pre-trained models outperform composition-specific EAM, glass-focused fine-tuning yields modest gains, and small-crystalline-cell specialization degrades disorder modeling.
infographic.watch_item: Results concern Cu–Zr–Al glasses; transfer to other alloy systems requires validation rather than assuming universal accuracy.
infographic.paper_title: Foundation interatomic potentials capture structural disorder in metallic glasses

title: Strain-Induced Tetragonal-to-Cubic Transition in MAPbI$_3$ from Machine-Learned Molecular Dynamics
authors: Daan Holleman, Luuk Klein Nagelvoort, Monica Morales-Masis, Linn Leppert
abstract: Metal-halide perovskites are promising photovoltaic absorbers whose optoelectronic properties are highly tunable. Epitaxial strain offers a route to stabilize desirable phases, tune band gaps, and reduce energetic disorder, but rational strain engineering requires predictive models. Static, zero-temperature "strained-bulk" density functional theory (DFT) calculations, successful for oxide perovskites, neglect the dynamic disorder and anharmonicity that govern halide perovskites at ambient temperature. Here, we show that molecular dynamics (MD) based on machine-learned force fields trained on-the-fly on DFT reproduces the structural and optoelectronic response of methylammonium (MA) lead iodide (MAPbI$_3$) to epitaxial strain at 300 K. We simulate bulk and free-standing slab models across experimentally accessible biaxial strains by locking the in-plane lattice vectors in nanosecond-long simulations. We predict a tetragonal-to-cubic transition at $\sim$0.5% tensile strain, marked by $c/a = 1$ and the loss of the $a^0a^0c^-$ tilting pattern, in agreement with experiments on epitaxial MAPbI$_3$ films on KCl. MA cations retain preferential orientations in the strain-induced cubic phase, unlike in its temperature-induced counterpart. Bulk and slab models yield consistent trends, with surface effects decaying within a few octahedral layers. Band gaps computed as ensemble averages over MD snapshots blue-shift under tensile strain, consistent with experiment, whereas static calculations on averaged structures predict a red shift. Our study positions MD with constrained lattice vectors as a method for predicting finite-temperature strain phase diagrams and guiding the epitaxial design of perovskite absorbers.

infographic.key_insight: Machine-learned molecular dynamics predicts that approximately 0.5% biaxial tensile strain drives MAPbI₃ from tetragonal to cubic at 300 K while retaining preferential molecular orientations.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Finite-temperature strain modeling can guide epitaxial design of perovskite absorbers by predicting phase stability and band-gap shifts that static calculations miss.
method: Train machine-learned force fields on-the-fly using DFT.
Run nanosecond bulk and free-standing slab simulations with constrained in-plane lattice vectors.
Track lattice ratios, octahedral tilts, molecular orientations, and snapshot-averaged band gaps.
infographic.evidence_signal: The predicted transition agrees with experiments on MAPbI₃ films on KCl, bulk and slab trends are consistent, and snapshot-averaged band gaps reproduce the experimental tensile-strain blue shift.
infographic.watch_item: Free-standing slabs do not explicitly capture substrate-interface chemistry, which may affect transferability to specific epitaxial systems.
infographic.paper_title: Strain-Induced Tetragonal-to-Cubic Transition in MAPbI$_3$ from Machine-Learned Molecular Dynamics

title: Self-supervised Clipped-objective Reinforcement Leaning Framework for Risk-aware Portfolio Management
authors: Zongshen Mu
abstract: Portfolio management involves balancing diverse financial assets, a critical yet challenging task in quantitative trading. Although deep reinforcement learning has emerged as an active research domain for solving complex sequential decision-making problems over the past decade, deploying reinforcement learning frameworks in non-stationary financial markets raises formidable difficulties. Most existing reinforcement learning-based portfolio management models fail to account for tick-level intraday market dynamics (e.g., order flow imbalances and liquidity fluctuations), which reflect rapid capital movements. Simultaneously, these models suffer from unstable learning processes due to reinforcement learning's inherent high variance. This paper presents a Self-supervised Clipped-objective Portfolio management framework (SCP), which addresses these limitations through a two-phase architecture. Market feature integration phase (application contribution) integrates micro-level market microstructure patterns with macro-level financial indicators to enhance sensitivity to intraday asset trend dynamics. Policy optimization Phase (AI contribution) employs intermediate asset state representations to derive optimal portfolio allocations via a self-supervised clipped-objective policy-learner, ensuring both effectiveness and computational efficiency. Extensive evaluations on three major index datasets from China's A-share market demonstrate that SCP's superior performance in balancing risk-return trade-offs compared to state-of-the-art baselines. Exploratory and ablation studies further validate the contributions of SCP's key components.

infographic.key_insight: SCP combines intraday market microstructure features with self-supervised, clipped-objective reinforcement learning to improve risk-aware portfolio allocation.
infographic.engineering_relevance: For quantitative trading systems rather than materials science, SCP targets sensitivity to fast market changes and greater stability in policy learning.
method: Integrate tick-level microstructure patterns with macro-level financial indicators.
Form intermediate asset-state representations for portfolio allocation.
Optimize allocations using a self-supervised, clipped-objective policy learner.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports superior risk–return performance against state-of-the-art baselines on three major Chinese A-share index datasets, with exploratory and ablation studies supporting component contributions.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract does not establish robustness to transaction costs, execution constraints, or markets beyond Chinese A-shares.
infographic.paper_title: Self-supervised Clipped-objective Reinforcement Leaning Framework for Risk-aware Portfolio Management

title: Lattice Thermal Conductivity of MgO and the MgSiO$_3$ Polymorphs Bridgmanite and Post-Perovskite at Lower-Mantle Conditions Using Fine-Tuned MACE Potentials
authors: Amrendra Kumar Tiwari, Sandro Jahn
abstract: Heat flow across the core-mantle boundary (CMB) depends on the lattice thermal conductivity ($κ_{\mathrm{latt}}$) of lowermost-mantle minerals, yet calculated CMB values for MgO differ severalfold, and high-temperature estimates of the conductivity increase across the bridgmanite-post-perovskite transition range from about 20 to 50%. Direct solutions of the linearized phonon Boltzmann transport equation (LBTE) require thousands of density functional theory (DFT) force evaluations per thermodynamic state. Here we replace these evaluations with phase-specific, fine-tuned MACE potentials for MgO, MgSiO3 bridgmanite (Pv), and MgSiO3 post-perovskite (PPv). The potentials reproduce DFT energies, forces, stresses, pressure-volume relations, and compressed-state phonons for all three phases. For MgO at 0 GPa, replacing MACE forces with DFT forces in otherwise identical transport calculations changes $κ_{\mathrm{latt}}$ by 0.2% at 300 K and 1.9% at 2000 K. PPv is 44-55% more conductive than Pv at the same pressure and temperature and strongly anisotropic, with $κ_{[100]}/κ_{[010]}$ ranging from 1.7 to 2.1. The quasi-harmonic phase boundary has a Clapeyron slope of $(7.4 \pm 0.1)$ MPa/K and intersects a model geotherm at 116.2 GPa and 2660 K, where the transition raises the silicate conductivity by 47%, to 8.6 W/(m K). Heating in the basal thermal boundary layer lowers the MgO and PPv conductivities to 37.3 and 6.7 W/(m K) at the CMB, where Hashin-Shtrikman bounds of 9.5-11.4 W/(m K) for an Fe-free aggregate of 80 vol% silicate and 20 vol% MgO encompass the 10 W/(m K) used in earlier heat-flow estimates. The density-temperature parameterizations provide an intrinsic end-member reference for lower-mantle thermal models.

infographic.key_insight: Fine-tuned MACE potentials predict that MgSiO3 post-perovskite conducts lattice heat 44–55% better than bridgmanite at matched lower-mantle pressures and temperatures.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The conductivity parameterizations support lower-mantle thermal models, with predicted core–mantle boundary aggregate values consistent with the 10 W/(m K) used in earlier heat-flow estimates.
method: Fine-tune phase-specific MACE potentials for MgO, bridgmanite, and post-perovskite.
Replace DFT force evaluations in linearized phonon Boltzmann transport calculations.
Combine quasi-harmonic phase-boundary calculations with aggregate conductivity bounds.
infographic.evidence_signal: For MgO at 0 GPa, substituting DFT for MACE forces in otherwise identical transport calculations changes conductivity by only 0.2% at 300 K and 1.9% at 2000 K.
infographic.watch_item: The aggregate estimates describe Fe-free end members; effects of realistic mantle chemistry require further evaluation.
infographic.paper_title: Lattice Thermal Conductivity of MgO and the MgSiO$_3$ Polymorphs Bridgmanite and Post-Perovskite at Lower-Mantle Conditions Using Fine-Tuned MACE Potentials

title: Photocatalytic Water Splitting in GeC/ReS$_2$ van der Waals Heterostructures
authors: Parisa Beyranvand, Ismaeil Abdolhosseini Sarsari, Noejung Park
abstract: Photocatalytic water splitting is considered as one of the most promising approaches for the green hydrogen production. But the rapid recombination of photogenerated electron-hole pairs severely inhibits its photocatalytic efficiency. Construction of van der Waals heterostructures is a good way to suppress this recombination. However, in staggered band heterostructures, the charge transfer could occur either through the type-II or the direct Z-scheme mechanism. Therefore it is very important to identify which mechanism is dominant. In the present work, we systematically study the GeC/ReS$_2$ heterostructure using first-principles density functional theory (DFT). The system exhibits good thermodynamic, dynamic and thermal stability and an indirect band gap of 1.38 eV which greatly enhances the visible-light absorption. We find that the direct Z-scheme mechanism is the dominant interfacial charge transfer by analysing band alignment and Gibbs free energy pathways. The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) can be driven spontaneously in the pH range $4 \le \text{pH} \le 14$ under light irradiation for both type-II and Z-scheme pathways but the energy barrier is much lower for the Z-scheme mechanism. Moreover, the type-II mechanism is not suitable for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), but the Z-scheme mechanism can promote HER well in the entire pH range ($0 \le \text{pH} \le 14$). Remarkably, the strain-free (pristine) condition exhibits a solar-to-hydrogen (STH) efficiency of 41.40\%, well above the 10\% threshold for commercial viability. The STH efficiency is further enhanced to 60.68\% under a tensile strain of +6\%. To summarise, the Z-scheme strain-tunable GeC/ReS$_2$ heterostructure is a promising and efficient photocatalyst for overall water splitting.

infographic.key_insight: DFT predicts that GeC/ReS₂ favors direct Z-scheme charge transfer, enabling overall photocatalytic water splitting with strain-tunable performance.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The heterostructure offers a computationally promising route to solar hydrogen production, with predicted solar-to-hydrogen efficiency increasing from 41.40% without strain to 60.68% at +6% tensile strain.
method: First-principles DFT assessment of stability and electronic structure.
Band-alignment and Gibbs free-energy analysis of type-II versus Z-scheme pathways.
Evaluation of pH-dependent water-splitting energetics and strain-dependent efficiency.
infographic.evidence_signal: Calculations indicate a 1.38 eV indirect band gap, favorable Z-scheme HER energetics at pH 0–14, and light-driven spontaneous OER at pH 4–14.
infographic.watch_item: The efficiencies are computational predictions; experimental validation must establish achievable strain, charge-transfer dynamics, and sustained catalytic performance.
infographic.paper_title: Photocatalytic Water Splitting in GeC/ReS$_2$ van der Waals Heterostructures

title: Origin of the anomalous shape of the $γ$-loop in paramagnetic Fe1-xCrx alloys from coupled Atomistic Spin Dynamics and ab initio Molecular Dynamics
authors: Joakim Stenborg, Davide Gambino, Björn Alling
abstract: The region of fcc stability in Fe-rich Fe-Cr alloys, the $γ$-loop, has an anomalous shape: at low temperatures, Cr addition initially stabilizes fcc, but above 8 at.% Cr it stabilizes bcc. At high temperatures, Cr always stabilizes bcc. This behavior reflects a delicate balance between magnetic, vibrational and configurational free-energy contributions that is challenging to capture from first principles. We investigate phase stability in Fe1-xCrx (x = 0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15) using coupled atomistic spin dynamics and ab initio molecular dynamics with thermodynamic integration. Gibbs free energy differences between fcc and bcc are calculated from 800 to 1800 K. Our calculations reproduce the experimental $γ$-loop and its compositional dependence, with near-quantitative accuracy for the $γ$-$δ$ transition. The $α$-$γ$ boundary, including its anomalous shape, is reproduced qualitatively, although transition temperatures are underestimated by approximately 200 K. Static calculations of magnetically ordered and disordered states provide an explanation: in ordered states, increasing Cr initially reduces the energetic preference for bcc over fcc, whereas in disordered states, Cr progressively stabilizes bcc at all compositions. Vibrational effects contribute to phase stability, while atomic short-range clustering at higher Cr content ($x \geq 0.15$) may explain the observed closing of the $γ$-loop from below. The simulations reveal finite Cr moments in the paramagnetic state, whose magnitudes depend on their local magnetic environment. The results demonstrate that the anomalous $γ$-loop arises from the interplay of magnetic energetics, magnetic disorder, lattice vibrations and chemical clustering, which must be treated on equal footing to capture phase stability from first principle

infographic.key_insight: The anomalous γ-loop in Fe–Cr alloys arises from competing magnetic, vibrational and chemical effects that change how Cr stabilizes fcc versus bcc structures.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Modeling these coupled effects can improve predictions of phase stability and transformation temperatures in Fe–Cr alloy design.
method: Coupled atomistic spin dynamics with ab initio molecular dynamics.
Used thermodynamic integration to calculate fcc–bcc Gibbs free-energy differences.
Compared static magnetically ordered and disordered states to isolate magnetic effects.
infographic.evidence_signal: Simulations at 0, 5, 10 and 15 at.% Cr over 800–1800 K reproduced the experimental γ-loop qualitatively, with near-quantitative accuracy for the γ–δ transition.
infographic.watch_item: The α–γ transition temperatures were underestimated by approximately 200 K, and clustering as a cause of loop closure remains tentative.
infographic.paper_title: Origin of the anomalous shape of the $γ$-loop in paramagnetic Fe1-xCrx alloys from coupled Atomistic Spin Dynamics and ab initio Molecular Dynamics

title: Solvent-Mediated Disintegration of a Vitrimer Network
authors: Manoj K Patel, Tarak K Patra
abstract: Vitrimers are dynamic polymer networks characterized by associative bond exchange, which enables topological rearrangement while preserving the overall network connectivity. However, how this dynamic connectivity evolves in the presence of a solvent, particularly as a function of temperature, remains poorly understood. Here, we employ hybrid molecular dynamics Monte Carlo simulations to elucidate the temperature-dependent restructuring and dissociation of vitrimer networks in solution. By constructing temperature composition phase diagrams, we demonstrate that the critical temperature for network dissolution increases nonlinearly with crosslink concentration. We find that the network disintegration begins well below the critical dissolution temperature, indicating that the loss of network connectivity can occur even before the onset of macroscopic dissolution. However, the network undergoes extensive restructuring around the critical temperature for a highly crosslinked system, resulting in the formation of numerous smaller, disconnected networks. Concurrently, the number of intrachain dynamic bonds increases with temperature. Interestingly, complete disintegration into individual polymer chains is not observed; instead, the solution comprises a broad distribution of smaller network fragments. These findings reveal the complex interplay between solvent-induced network disintegration and dynamic bond redistribution, providing molecular level insights into the dissolution of vitrimer networks and their potential for solvent assisted recycling.

infographic.key_insight: Solvent-exposed vitrimer networks begin losing connectivity below the critical dissolution temperature and form smaller network fragments rather than fully separating into individual polymer chains.
infographic.engineering_relevance: These findings could guide solvent-assisted vitrimer recycling by linking temperature and crosslink concentration to network fragmentation.
method: Hybrid molecular dynamics–Monte Carlo simulations
Temperature–composition phase diagrams
Analysis of network fragmentation and dynamic bond redistribution
infographic.evidence_signal: Simulations show that the critical dissolution temperature rises nonlinearly with crosslink concentration, while intrachain dynamic bonds increase with temperature.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract reports simulation results without experimental validation, so transferability to practical recycling conditions remains uncertain.
infographic.paper_title: Solvent-Mediated Disintegration of a Vitrimer Network

title: Computing hydration free energies and crystalline solubility of drug-like molecules with MACE
authors: J. Harry Moore, Paul Mortenson, Davide Branduardi, Pavel Buslaev, Javier Antorán, Laurence Midgley
abstract: Accurate prediction of thermodynamic solubility is critical in drug discovery, where it influences oral bioavailability and drives decisions in formulation chemistry. First-principles calculations of intrinsic solubility offer the potential to achieve superior generalization to existing direct, data-driven predictors, which often suffer significant performance degradation outside of their training distribution. Whilst free energy perturbation calculations provide a rigorous framework to estimate these quantities, their accuracy is typically limited by the quality of the empirical force field used. In this work, we present a computational workflow driven by the MACE family of machine learning interatomic potentials to compute the solubility of neutral drug-like molecules. We introduce $λ$-MACE, a potential optimised for condensed-phase free energy calculations, which enables hydration free energy calculations at experimental accuracy on an evaluation set of 70 compounds from the FreeSolv database selected for their relevance to medicinal chemistry. We further combine these hydration free energy calculations with sublimation free energy calculations to predict crystalline solubility given a known experimental crystal structure, on an additional set of 10 compounds. We achieve state-of-the-art performance for each leg of the calculation, with experimental accuracy for the hydration leg, and accuracy competitive with industry-standard DFT for the sublimation leg. However, the overall errors after combining both legs lead to accuracy of 1.53 log units. This is significantly above the experimental accuracy (0.17-0.6 log units). Closing this gap will require substantially tighter accuracy in each leg, on the order of half of chemical accuracy (0.5 kcal/mol), with crystalline thermodynamics the hardest remaining challenge.

infographic.key_insight: λ-MACE enables experimentally accurate hydration free energies for drug-like molecules, but combined hydration and sublimation errors still limit crystalline solubility predictions.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Physics-based solubility prediction could support drug formulation decisions, provided crystalline thermodynamics can be modeled more accurately.
method: Optimize λ-MACE for condensed-phase free energy calculations.
Compute hydration and sublimation free energies using MACE-driven calculations.
Combine both contributions to predict solubility from known experimental crystal structures.
infographic.evidence_signal: Evaluation covered 70 medicinally relevant FreeSolv compounds for hydration and 10 additional compounds for crystalline solubility, yielding solubility accuracy of 1.53 log units versus experimental accuracy of 0.17–0.6 log units.
infographic.watch_item: Reaching experimental solubility accuracy requires roughly 0.5 kcal/mol accuracy in each free energy leg, with crystalline thermodynamics the hardest remaining challenge.
infographic.paper_title: Computing hydration free energies and crystalline solubility of drug-like molecules with MACE

title: Magnetically Guided Sequential Multi-Filler Alignment Enables Anisotropic Heat Pathways in Stretchable Composites for Soft Electronics
authors: Altynay Kaidarova, Viktor Naenen, Isidro Florenciano, Ruben Windey, Xiaoyan Qing, Laurens Snels
abstract: Stretchable, skin-conformal electronics demand thermal interface materials that combine high through-plane heat transport with mechanical softness and lateral electrical insulation. In particle-filled composites, these requirements are typically antagonistic. Heat transport is governed not only by the intrinsic thermal conductivity of the fillers but, more critically, by thermal resistance at the interparticle interface. As the interparticle distance is reduced by increasing the particle content, mechanical reinforcement and in-plane electrical conductivity become unavoidable. The existing particle alignment processing strategies result in inefficient uncoupling of multifunctionality. Here, we present a hierarchical two-step process strategy to induce strong conductivity anisotropy in a soft composite. First, an align-before-blend process forms a scaffold of magnetically aligned nickel (Ni) microparticles in air before polymer infiltration. The absence of the viscous elastomer matrix during the particle alignment facilitates handling large amounts of particles, which assemble into highly ordered and densely packed vertical heat-conduction pathways. Second, a liquid metal (LM)/Ni mixture is infiltrated into the aligned scaffold to bridge interparticle gaps, minimizing interparticle thermal resistance. The composite reaches 7.5 W/(m K) through-plane thermal conductivity with lateral electrical conductivity below $10^{-12}$ S/m and ultrasoft mechanical compliance (approximately 160 kPa), enabling coupling layers in thermoelectric generators and finger-mounted heat-spreading pads for wearable technologies.

infographic.key_insight: Sequential magnetic alignment and liquid-metal bridging create vertical heat pathways in a soft composite while preserving lateral electrical insulation.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The composite offers a compliant thermal interface for skin-conformal electronics, thermoelectric generators, and wearable heat-spreading pads.
method: Magnetically align Ni microparticles in air before polymer infiltration to form densely packed vertical pathways.
Infiltrate a liquid-metal/Ni mixture into the scaffold to bridge interparticle gaps and reduce thermal resistance.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports through-plane thermal conductivity of 7.5 W/(m K), lateral electrical conductivity below 10⁻¹² S/m, and mechanical compliance characterized by approximately 160 kPa.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract does not establish whether thermal performance and electrical insulation persist under repeated stretching.
infographic.paper_title: Magnetically Guided Sequential Multi-Filler Alignment Enables Anisotropic Heat Pathways in Stretchable Composites for Soft Electronics

title: Interpretable identification of constitutive parameter field for three-dimensional heterogeneous and graded hyperelastic materials from full-field displacements
authors: Kanhaiya Lal Chaurasiya, Vaskar Halder, Prajyot Patil, Gaurav Navnath Shinde, Debashish Das, Akshay Joshi
abstract: The inverse problem of identifying spatially varying material properties of heterogeneous solids using experimentally available displacement fields and boundary reaction forces alone remains challenging. Being able to characterize heterogeneous and graded solids would be advantageous in the design and manufacturing of functionally graded materials and composites. Additionally, an efficient technique for identifying heterogeneous material properties from in vivo measurements would be useful in biomedical contexts to characterize heterogeneous biological tissues. Although several techniques developed over the past two decades have addressed inverse identification for homogeneous materials, including linear elastic, hyperelastic, viscoelastic, and elastoplastic solids, comparatively fewer studies have considered heterogeneous and graded materials. Furthermore, several recent approaches to characterizing heterogeneous and graded materials employ parameter-heavy, deep learning-based frameworks trained to enforce force equilibrium at specified collocation points within the material. In this work, we propose an interpretable and time-efficient framework that predicts the three-dimensional relative spatial variation of a constitutive parameter field for multiple parameters of a heterogeneous hyperelastic material, using only displacement-field data. In this work, we validate our framework on 3D synthetic and 2D experimental benchmarks involving heterogeneous, graded, and anisotropic hyperelastic materials. By leveraging the linear nature of the inverse problem for hyperelastic materials and directly optimizing for the constitutive parameters at the finite-element level, we achieve acceptable prediction accuracy with significantly lower computational time compared to recently reported deep-learning-based frameworks.

infographic.key_insight: An interpretable finite-element inverse framework identifies relative spatial variations in multiple constitutive parameters of 3D heterogeneous hyperelastic materials from displacement fields alone.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Mapping material-property variations could support characterization of graded composites and heterogeneous biological tissues.
method: Leverages linearity of the hyperelastic inverse problem in the constitutive parameters.
Optimizes constitutive parameters directly at the finite-element level.
Avoids parameter-heavy deep-learning models.
infographic.evidence_signal: Validation on 3D synthetic and 2D experimental benchmarks covers heterogeneous, graded, and anisotropic hyperelastic materials, with reported acceptable accuracy and substantially lower computational time than recent deep-learning frameworks.
infographic.watch_item: The framework recovers relative parameter variations; absolute property calibration and robustness to noisy 3D experimental displacement data require further assessment.
infographic.paper_title: Interpretable identification of constitutive parameter field for three-dimensional heterogeneous and graded hyperelastic materials from full-field displacements

title: Exact subtraction of electron self-interaction from the Kohn-Sham equations
authors: J. E. Ingall, Alister J. Page
abstract: The self-interaction error (SIE) of Kohn-Sham density functional theory (KS-DFT) leads to a non-physical, non-linear dependence of an orbital's energy on its own fractional occupation [Dabo et al., Phys. Rev. B, 82:115121, 2010]. The generalized Koopmans condition (GKC) ensures an atomic orbital's eigenenergy is independent of its fractional occupation$-$ and is free of self-interaction. The constrained search of the Levy spin-density-functional theory yields orbital densities and delivers the ground-state energy to generalize the Hohenberg-Kohn theorems. In this work, the electron density of the Kohn-Sham equations is constrained to be orbital-density dependent, with a total energy functional linear with respect to variation of its orbital densities. That is, the KS multiplicative effective potential $v_{\text{s}}[{n}]$ for an orbital $\varphi_i[{n}]$ is constrained to a functional $v_{\text{eff}}[{n - n_i}]$. The result complies with the generalized Koopmans condition (GKC). This approach improves LDA and GGA mean absolute errors (MAEs) in fundamental band gaps by $\sim$ 1 eV, with respect to KS-DFT. Equations free of electron self-interaction provide the basis for improvements in the accuracy, efficiency, and simplicity of density functional theories.

infographic.key_insight: Constraining each orbital’s effective potential to depend on the electron density excluding that orbital removes its self-interaction and satisfies the generalized Koopmans condition.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The approach could improve fundamental band-gap predictions for materials using LDA and GGA density functional approximations.
method: Constrain the effective potential for orbital i to depend on n − n_i.
Require total-energy linearity with respect to orbital-density variations.
Enforce orbital eigenenergies independent of their own fractional occupations.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports an approximately 1 eV reduction in fundamental band-gap mean absolute errors for LDA and GGA relative to standard KS-DFT.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract does not specify benchmark materials, computational overhead, or convergence behavior for the orbital-dependent potentials.
infographic.paper_title: Exact subtraction of electron self-interaction from the Kohn-Sham equations

title: AI-human hybrid conversations: Can AI Agents Improve Discourse Quality?
authors: Ishita Chakraborty, Xingjian You, Shrabastee Banerjee
abstract: Conversations are central to how people exchange information, share experiences, and develop collective understanding. Yet, across conversational settings, discussions often suffer from uneven participation, unanswered contributions, and a narrow range of perspectives. As generative AI agents increasingly participate alongside humans, hybrid human-AI conversations present a new opportunity to address these challenges. We investigate whether AI agents can serve as catalysts for human interaction, improving conversational engagement and broadening collective discourse. We develop a framework for introducing generic and persona-conditioned AI agents into evolving discussions and evaluate it through two complementary studies. First, using agent-based simulations grounded in Reddit discussions across four domains, we find that AI-generated conversations are more positive and less toxic than human conversations, but substantially less semantically diverse. Persona conditioning produces more human-like contributions and narrows this diversity gap, while increasing the representation of underrepresented personas can shift which perspectives emerge without necessarily increasing overall diversity. Second, we conduct a pre-registered experiment with 221 participants across nine discussion threads, comparing human-only conversations with those involving generic or persona-conditioned AI agents. We find that AI participation increases responsiveness, reduces unanswered contributions, and broadens the range of ideas expressed by human participants, even though the AI agents themselves do not fully reproduce human conversational diversity. These findings suggest that the value of hybrid human-AI conversations lies not simply in the content AI agents generate, but also in their potential to stimulate more responsive and diverse interactions among humans.

infographic.key_insight: AI agents can make human discussions more responsive and broaden human contributions, despite generating less semantically diverse conversations themselves.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The findings may inform AI facilitators for collaborative engineering discussions, but the study does not evaluate materials discovery.
method: Introduced generic and persona-conditioned AI agents into evolving discussions.
Ran agent-based simulations grounded in Reddit discussions across four domains.
Compared human-only and hybrid discussions in a pre-registered participant experiment.
infographic.evidence_signal: Simulations found more positive, less toxic but less diverse AI conversations; an experiment with 221 participants across nine threads found improved responsiveness, fewer unanswered contributions, and broader human ideas.
infographic.watch_item: Persona conditioning narrowed the diversity gap, but increasing underrepresented personas did not necessarily increase overall diversity.
infographic.paper_title: AI-human hybrid conversations: Can AI Agents Improve Discourse Quality?

title: Atomistic insight into defect-mediated boron redistribution and high-temperature strengthening in TiAl alloys
authors: Xiang Meng, Shuhei Shinzato, Zhiqiang Zhao, Linfeng Yu, Jian Guo, Liangli Chu
abstract: Boron (B) microalloying can effectively refine microstructures of as-cast TiAl alloys and regulate their mechanical properties. Yet, how dilute B exists in TiAl and interacts with defects and how these interactions govern high-temperature deformation remain elusive. Here, we systematically elucidate defect-mediated B redistribution in TiAl alloys and its consequences for their deformation using hybrid grand-canonical Monte Carlo/molecular dynamics simulations augmented with a newly developed high-fidelity machine-learning potential. As a typical product of B microalloying, borides are markedly stiffer than the TiAl matrix and act as brittle reinforcing phases, while borides/matrix interfacial adhesion depends on surface termination and stacking sequence. In the bulk, interstitial B tends to be trapped at Ti-rich octahedral sites by high migration barriers but can kinetically evolve into substitutional dopants upon approaching Al vacancies. Increased tensile stress and vacancy concentration further promote B enrichment in the bulk. B is enriched at semi-coherent $γ/α_2$ boundaries and preferentially partitions into the $α_2$ phase. In polycrystalline TiAl, B accumulates primarily in disordered regions, raising the average flow stress by 9.4% at 1 at.% B and 900 K. This strengthening is accompanied by reduced shear strain accumulation. Simulated microstructural evolution and stacking-fault energetics indicate that B impedes dislocation glide via local pinning and suppresses deformation twinning, thereby increasing resistance to plastic deformation. By linking solute redistribution to defect interactions and deformation, these findings establish an atomistic framework for understanding and designing high-performance alloys based on interstitial solutes.

infographic.key_insight: Boron redistributes to defects in TiAl alloys, locally pinning dislocations and suppressing deformation twinning to strengthen the material at high temperature.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Controlling boron content and defect populations could help design stronger high-temperature TiAl alloys, while accounting for brittle borides and interface-dependent adhesion.
method: Hybrid grand-canonical Monte Carlo/molecular dynamics simulations
Newly developed high-fidelity machine-learning interatomic potential
Atomistic analysis of boron segregation, defect interactions, and deformation
infographic.evidence_signal: In simulated polycrystalline TiAl at 900 K, 1 at.% boron increased average flow stress by 9.4% and reduced shear strain accumulation.
infographic.watch_item: The strengthening result is simulation-based; experimental validation and assessment across processing conditions are needed before alloy-design deployment.
infographic.paper_title: Atomistic insight into defect-mediated boron redistribution and high-temperature strengthening in TiAl alloys

title: Diagnostic Accuracy Is Not Deployment Value: Decision-Aligned Reliability Evaluation for Foundation MLIPs in Materials Discovery
authors: Harry Sevi, Joonatan E. M. Laulainen
abstract: In AI-guided materials discovery, machine-learning models increasingly decide which candidate materials should receive expensive first-principles or experimental evaluation. Standard reliability metrics such as uncertainty, calibration, novelty, and ranking accuracy evaluate properties of the predictions, but success on these metrics does not necessarily imply a better downstream screening decision. We study this mismatch for foundation machine-learned interatomic potentials (MACE-MP, CHGNet, Orb V3) used to rank candidate crystal structures before DFT verification. We evaluate three representative reliability interventions (novelty detection, sparse DFT calibration, and chemistry-level ranking audits) using a deployment objective that measures how much DFT can be avoided while maintaining a required recall of near-hull candidates. Across all three, a reliability signal can succeed on its immediate target without improving the final screening decision: novelty detects distribution shift but weakly ranks failure severity; calibration can improve pooled ranking metrics while leaving screening unchanged or degrading it; and sparse audits identify MLIP-chemistry combinations with poor ranking reliability without yielding a robustly beneficial routing policy. A two-oracle analysis further shows that the source of failure depends on the screening decision itself: under formation-energy screening, even perfect knowledge of average ranking reliability can select the wrong model, whereas in the evaluated hull-aligned variant the oracle target becomes decision-aligned but finite-budget audits still fail to realize the value. Reliability should be evaluated relative to the decision it supports: the relevant question is not whether a model is uncertain or inaccurate, but whether acquiring and acting on additional information will improve the final discovery decision enough to justify its cost.

infographic.key_insight: Better reliability diagnostics do not necessarily improve materials screening; their value depends on whether they reduce DFT evaluations while preserving required recall of near-hull candidates.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Evaluate MLIP reliability interventions against screening outcomes and information-acquisition costs, not prediction metrics alone.
method: Rank candidate crystal structures with MACE-MP, CHGNet, and Orb V3 before DFT verification.
Test novelty detection, sparse DFT calibration, and chemistry-level ranking audits.
Measure DFT savings at required near-hull recall and use two-oracle analysis to diagnose decision alignment.
infographic.evidence_signal: Across the three interventions, improved diagnostic performance did not reliably translate into better screening: novelty weakly ranked failure severity, calibration could leave screening unchanged or worse, and audits did not yield robustly beneficial routing.
infographic.watch_item: Results depend on the screening objective: perfect average-ranking information can misguide formation-energy screening, while finite-budget audits still failed to realize oracle value in the evaluated hull-aligned variant.
infographic.paper_title: Diagnostic Accuracy Is Not Deployment Value: Decision-Aligned Reliability Evaluation for Foundation MLIPs in Materials Discovery

title: Wannier-Based Low-Energy Electronic Structure Analysis of $λ$-(STF)$_2$GaCl$_4$
authors: Arifa D. Agustin, Aulia A. Firdaus, Fathan M. Santana, Shuhei Fukuoka, Atsushi Kawamoto, Muhammad R. Ramadhan
abstract: The low-energy electronic structures of $λ$-(BETS)$_2$GaCl$_4$ and $λ$-(STF)$_2$GaCl$_4$ were investigated using density functional theory (DFT) and maximally localized Wannier functions (MLWFs). For $λ$-(STF)$_2$GaCl$_4$, DFT-selected and directly XRD-refined structural models were compared before and after fixed-lattice relaxation. Their initially different near-Fermi-level electronic structures become similar after relaxation. Relative to BETS, relaxed STF has a narrower frontier bandwidth while retaining a substantial dimerization energy scale. Two MLWFs were constructed for each selected unrelaxed structure to represent the upper frontier bands, with total spreads of 36.708 Å$^2$ for BETS and 37.578 Å$^2$ for STF. The Wannier-derived transfer integrals show a pronounced reduction of $t_{d1}$ from 51 meV in BETS to 6.5 meV in STF, indicating selective modification of the low-energy electronic connectivity.

infographic.key_insight: Relaxed λ-(STF)₂GaCl₄ has a narrower frontier bandwidth than its BETS counterpart while retaining substantial dimerization, and unrelaxed-structure Wannier models reveal selectively weakened electronic connectivity.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Structure-sensitive bandwidths and transfer integrals help parameterize low-energy models of molecular conductors.
method: Use DFT to compare BETS and STF electronic structures.
Compare DFT-selected and XRD-refined STF models before and after fixed-lattice relaxation.
Construct two maximally localized Wannier functions per selected unrelaxed structure for the upper frontier bands.
infographic.evidence_signal: The STF structural models yield similar near-Fermi electronic structures after relaxation; unrelaxed Wannier models give total spreads of 36.708 Å² for BETS and 37.578 Å² for STF, with t_d1 decreasing from 51 to 6.5 meV.
infographic.watch_item: The reported Wannier transfer integrals describe selected unrelaxed structures and should not be assumed to represent the relaxed structures.
infographic.paper_title: Wannier-Based Low-Energy Electronic Structure Analysis of $λ$-(STF)$_2$GaCl$_4$

title: Native vacancy energetics and association in TiN and CrN: chemical potential dependence, clustering, and surface effects
authors: Barsha Bhattacharjee, Emilia Olsson
abstract: Native vacancy populations in transition-metal nitride coatings reflect vacancy formation, association, and depth-dependent stability. Using density functional theory (DFT), we compare these effects in rocksalt TiN and CrN in bulk and at (001) surfaces, within phase-stability-constrained chemical potential ranges. In TiN, $V_\mathrm{N}$ is favoured under N-poor and $V_\mathrm{Ti}$ under N-rich conditions; in CrN, $V_\mathrm{N}$ remains preferred throughout its stability range. Association energies are referenced to corresponding isolated vacancies where positive values mean association lowers the energy and negative values favour separation. Mean bulk association energies for mixed metal-nitrogen pairs are $+0.132$ eV in TiN and $+1.053$ eV in CrN. At (001) surfaces, $V_\mathrm{N}$ in TiN prefers the surface and $V_\mathrm{Ti}$ the first subsurface layer. In CrN, $V_\mathrm{N}$ has similar formation energies at the surface and first subsurface layer, with a slight preference for the latter; $V_\mathrm{Cr}$ slightly prefers the second subsurface layer. Surface cluster energies are referenced to separated vacancies at their preferred depths. The compact $2V_\mathrm{Ti}+2V_\mathrm{N}$ cluster in TiN has favourable association in bulk ($+0.217$ eV per vacancy) but unfavourable association at the surface ($-0.346$ eV per vacancy). By contrast, $2V_\mathrm{Cr}+2V_\mathrm{N}$ in CrN remains stabilised, with its association energy decreasing from $+1.188$ to $+0.431$ eV per vacancy. CrN's stronger association occurs without larger structural distortions and is accompanied by distinct Cr-centred magnetic responses.

infographic.key_insight: DFT predicts stronger vacancy association in CrN than TiN, with compact mixed-vacancy clusters remaining stabilised at CrN surfaces but becoming unfavourable at TiN surfaces.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Material choice, nitrogen chemical potential, and proximity to surfaces can influence vacancy populations and clustering in TiN and CrN coatings.
method: DFT comparison of native vacancies in rocksalt TiN and CrN bulk and (001) surfaces.
Formation energies evaluated within phase-stability-constrained chemical potential ranges.
Association energies referenced to isolated vacancies, using preferred depths for surface comparisons.
infographic.evidence_signal: Compact two-metal/two-nitrogen vacancy clusters have bulk-to-surface association energies of +0.217 to −0.346 eV per vacancy in TiN and +1.188 to +0.431 eV per vacancy in CrN, where positive values favour association.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract reports energetic preferences, not experimental validation or vacancy migration kinetics, so clustering rates in operating coatings remain uncertain.
infographic.paper_title: Native vacancy energetics and association in TiN and CrN: chemical potential dependence, clustering, and surface effects
